_README: Quarterly/annual research-monitor events, calendar-triggered — mirrors calendar.json's schema and trigger vocabulary exactly (read by the same collect_calendar() in main.py, just pointed at this file instead) so there's one mental model for both. Kept separate from calendar.json on purpose: these are research-monitoring concerns (Stage 3 of the research pipeline, see 'monitorable source list.md'), not personal/seasonal newspaper events like the Booker Prize or FOMC dates. Rendered into research.html alongside the daily-pulled sources, not into the main daily calendar section. Same trigger types as calendar.json: 'first_tuesday_monthly', 'annual_window' (months list — reused here for quarterly cadences by listing 3-4 months, since there's no separate 'quarterly' trigger type; one vocabulary, not two), 'manual' (explicit YYYY-MM-DD dates). Added 2026-09-15/16.

events.label: Chicago Fed AgLetter (7th District farmland values & credit)
events.notes: Published Feb/May/Aug/Nov, covering IN/IL/IA/WI/MI. No confirmed RSS — checked 2026-09-15, chicagofed.org has no obvious feed for individual publication series; manual check via the URL. Exact 2026 release dates (Feb 12, May 14, Aug 13, Nov 12) come from the Chicago Fed's own page, checked 2026-09-29; the 'manual' trigger marks the event due within 1 day of each date. 2027 dates are not published yet; add them once the Chicago Fed lists them.

events.label: Ed Zitron — quarterly review (AI-economics bear case)
events.notes: Moved 2026-09-29 from the weekly feed at the maintainer's decision: one author, quality varies within a post (sharp analysis and long rants), the free text is largely a subscription pitch, and the analysis is paywalled. He is kept on trial, checked once a quarter instead of weekly. On the window, read the past quarter's free posts, note which cited a checkable figure or source (e.g. the Sept 29 post quoting Fidelity's Jurien Timmer), and log a standard_review line with a keep or cut verdict; a cut needs that pattern across quarters. Feed for the read: https://www.wheresyoured.at/rss/ (posts titled 'Premium:' are paywalled).

events.label: Fed Distributional Financial Accounts (wealth shares by percentile)
events.notes: Updated ~10-11 weeks after each quarter end (Q4 data ~mid-March, Q1 ~mid-June, Q2 ~mid-September, Q3 ~mid-December) — approximated here by release-month, not quarter-end month. No RSS found for this specific release; the Fed's .../dfa/announcements/ page is the closest thing to a change feed but isn't machine-readable. Manual check.

events.label: St. Louis Fed — Ag Finance Monitor
events.notes: Eighth District quarterly ag credit/land-value survey, roughly aligned with the Chicago Fed's release cadence. Exact release months not separately confirmed — using the same Feb/May/Aug/Nov approximation as Chicago Fed pending a closer check; correct this if a Tuesday session finds the actual pattern differs.

events.label: Indiana State Climate Office — Climate INformer newsletter
events.notes: Quarterly newsletter, email-only (subscribe via mailimages.purdue.edu), no RSS. Exact quarter-start months not confirmed against a real issue calendar — using calendar-quarter starts as a placeholder; correct once actual issue months are observed. Low cost of being wrong either way given the 21-day lookahead window.

events.label: USDA NASS Land Values annual summary & Cash Rents
events.notes: State/US estimates release first week of August; county-level cash rents late August. Reuses the same Quick Stats API + NASS_API_KEY already proven working in nass_crop_progress_scrape.py (see nass_land_values_scrape.py). Verified live 2026-09-15 via a manual out-of-window run: Farm Real Estate Value and Cropland Cash Rent both confirmed working ($8,600/acre and $232/acre for Indiana 2026, both plausible). One real bug found and fixed during verification — a guessed statisticcat_desc ('RENT, CASH, CROPLAND') doesn't exist and the API 400'd on it; the real field is statisticcat_desc 'EXPENSE' with class_desc carrying the cropland/pastureland distinction.

events.label: Chicago Fed National Activity Index (CFNAI) - recession-risk reading
events.notes: Added 2026-09-29. Weighted composite of 85 monthly indicators; the Chicago Fed's own reading rule is what to record: CFNAI-MA3 below -0.70 after an expansion is associated with an increasing likelihood of recession (NBER-dated history). The current-data page draws its chart by script, but each release's headline text (index value, MA3, diffusion index) is a plain HTML file at the url above, refreshed at every release (checked 2026-09-29: last-modified Sep 21, 8:30 a.m. ET release day). There is no RSS and no monthly release PDF (only background PDFs), so this is a due-date reminder, not a scraper: on the day, read the MA3 from that text and record it as a calendar_reading in research_data/curation_log.jsonl. Release dates copied from the Chicago Fed's own data-release-calendar page on 2026-09-29 (8:30 a.m. ET): Oct 26 (September data), Nov 23 (October), Dec 21 (November); 2026 already released: Jan 26, Feb 23, Mar 23, Apr 23, May 26, Jun 25, Jul 23, Aug 24, Sep 21. 2027 dates are not published yet; add them each December. Ranked below the Beige Book: a mechanical index with no prose, so no honest-null statement, but it is the direct recession-threshold metric. The 'manual' trigger marks the event due within 1 day of each date.

events.label: Iowa State (CARD) Land Value Survey
events.notes: Results published mid-December (2024 survey: Dec 17). No RSS found for Ag Decision Maker or the CARD Farmland Portal — checked 2026-09-15. Manual check via URL.

events.label: World Inequality Report / WID.world annual update
events.notes: WIR 2026 was released Dec 10, 2025 (lead author Ricardo Gomez-Carrera with Piketty/Chancel) — the full flagship report is periodic (2018, 2022, 2026 so far, not strictly annual), but the WID.world database itself updates annually and December is the observed pattern for both. No RSS confirmed for wid.world — manual check.

events.label: USFS + Michigan DNR Forest Health Highlights (annual, spring)
events.notes: Michigan DNR's 2025 edition released late April 2026; USFS state-level Forest Health Highlights PDFs (IN_FHH, MI_FHH) follow a similar spring window. No RSS for either — PDF releases, calendar-checked. Covers both the Michigan DNR and USFS items from the source plan's Stage 3 list under one entry since they land in the same window and both lack automation; check both URLs when this fires.

events.label: Ownership Works — annual Impact Report
events.notes: The 2025 Impact Report's own site metadata indicates a ~May 2026 publication date — used as the best available signal for timing, not a confirmed fixed release month (checked 2026-09-15, no explicit 'always published in X' statement found). Revisit this month if a future year's report lands noticeably differently.

events.label: IEA Energy and AI (global data-centre electricity demand)
events.notes: Global benchmark for data-centre power. The April 2025 report put 2024 data-centre demand at about 415 TWh and projected about 945 TWh by 2030 (Base Case), with the US and China about 80% of the growth (figures from search-result summaries of the report, 2026-09-29; not read on iea.org). UNVERIFIED: iea.org returns 403 to scripted fetches (curl and WebFetch, 2026-09-29), so no feed, scraper or next-release date could be checked, and whether IEA issues an annual update or an Energy and AI observatory refresh is not confirmed; April is a guess from the 2025 release month. Check the URL by hand in a normal browser. Companion to epoch_datacenters (dated global snapshot).

events.label: LBNL US Data Center Energy Usage Report (national benchmark)
events.notes: National benchmark for data-centre electricity. The 2024 report was published 2024-12-19 (estimates back to 2014, scenarios to 2028: 6.7-12.0% of US electricity by 2028); a 2025 Update exists (11.8% of US electricity by 2030, range 9.5-15.3%; per search-result summaries 2026-09-29, not read directly). Release dates are irregular, and eta.lbl.gov returns 403 to scripted fetches, so nothing here is verified beyond the search listing; December is the month of the 2024 release, not a schedule. Check https://datacenters.lbl.gov/publications by hand and log the published figure when a new edition appears.

events.label: Fed Survey of Consumer Finances — 2025 results (one-time watch)
events.notes: Triennial survey (2019, 2022, 2025); fieldwork began March 2025, so results are expected late 2026. This entry deliberately recurs every Oct-Dec via annual_window (there's no 'fire once ever' trigger type in this vocabulary) — once the 2025 results are actually published and the Tuesday session has synthesized them, DELETE this entry rather than letting it keep firing every autumn for a release that already happened.

deprioritized.note: Investigated 2026-09-15/16, deliberately not given a calendar entry. Same documentation standard as research_sources.json's deprioritized section — revisit only on new information.

sources.label: Indiana Woodland Steward newsletter (~3x/year)
sources.reason: No fixed release window to build a calendar trigger around (irregular, ~3 issues/year). New issues were surfaced by the purdue_gotnature feed until that source was cut on 2026-10-06; nothing tracks it now. Revisit only if the maintainer wants it watched.

sources.label: NCEO Employee Ownership Report / annual research
sources.reason: No confirmed fixed release month found (checked 2026-09-15) — 'Employee Ownership Month' every October is an awareness campaign, not a confirmed publication date for NCEO's own research reports, and the bulk of NCEO's newsletter/survey content is paywalled behind membership anyway (per the original source plan). Not worth a guessed calendar window on top of low automatable value. If the user has an NCEO membership and wants this tracked, revisit with real subscriber access rather than public-page guessing.

calendar_only_ai_grid_energy.note: These Stage 2 sources have no usable RSS/API and no NCEO-style paid-access reasoning to skip entirely — they're tracked as recurring manual-check calendar entries above are for quarterly/annual items, but their cadence (monthly) doesn't fit calendar.json's vocabulary well (there's no clean 'monthly, any day' trigger — annual_window with all 12 months would technically work but reads as a hack). Documented here instead of silently dropped; add proper calendar entries (or build automation) if/when it's worth the added complexity.

sources.label: EIA Electric Power Monthly
sources.reason: EIA has a real Open Data API (api.eia.gov) with monthly electric-power-operations data, but it requires a free API key that isn't currently available as a secret in this repo (unlike NOAA_TOKEN and NASS_API_KEY, which were already provisioned). EIA's RSS feed guesses (eia.gov/electricity/data/rss/epm.xml, eia.gov/rss/*.xml) all 404 or redirect to a generic HTML page — checked 2026-09-15. If the user wants this automated, get an EIA API key (free, instant signup at eia.gov/opendata/) and this can follow the same api-key-scrape-module pattern as NOAA/NASS.

sources.label: LBNL U.S. Data Center Energy Usage Report
sources.reason: Confirmed 2026-09-15 (via web search, since eta.lbl.gov 403s direct fetches — Cloudflare bot-blocked) that a successor to the Dec 2024 report already exists: the '2025 Update', published June 2026, revising the 2028 data-center electricity share estimate up to 9.5-15.3% (central 11.8%) from the original report's 6.7-12% by 2028. No RSS; irregular publication cadence (~18 months between the two editions so far). Worth a periodic manual check of eta.lbl.gov/publications, not a fixed-month calendar entry given only two data points on cadence.

sources.label: Iowa State — Ag Decision Maker (monthly newsletter)
sources.reason: No RSS found (checked 2026-09-15: /rss.xml, /feed both 404). Email-subscription only. Monthly manual check.

sources.label: Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City — Ag Credit Survey / Ag Bulletin
sources.reason: No RSS found on kansascityfed.org (checked 2026-09-15, no rss/feed links on the homepage or guessed paths). Quarterly survey plus rolling Bulletin articles; manual check.
